questions.question: Who are Australia's first inhabitants?
options: The convicts of the First Fleet
Free settlers from Great Britain and Ireland
The Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples
questions.answer: The Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples
questions.explanation: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples are Australia's first inhabitants and have the oldest continuous cultures in the world.

questions.question: According to the archaeological record, when did Aboriginal peoples arrive in Australia?
questions.answer: Between 65,000 and 40,000 years ago
questions.explanation: The archaeological record places the arrival of Aboriginal peoples between 65,000 and 40,000 years ago. Aboriginal peoples' own creation stories begin with the beginning of time.

questions.question: Where are Torres Strait Islander people from?
options: Islands between the northern tip of Queensland and Papua New Guinea
Islands off the coast of Western Australia
questions.answer: Islands between the northern tip of Queensland and Papua New Guinea
questions.explanation: Torres Strait Islander people come from the islands between the northern tip of Queensland and Papua New Guinea.

questions.question: Historically, Aboriginal people are from which parts of Australia?
questions.answer: Mainland Australia and Tasmania
questions.explanation: Historically, Aboriginal people are from mainland Australia and Tasmania; Torres Strait Islander people are from the Torres Strait islands.

questions.question: What is said about Australia's Indigenous cultures?
options: They are all identical to one another
They are the oldest continuous cultures in the world
questions.answer: They are the oldest continuous cultures in the world
questions.explanation: Indigenous cultures are the oldest continuous cultures in the world, are diverse, and are an important part of Australia's national identity.

questions.question: How do Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples express their deep connection with the land?
options: Through their stories, art and dance
questions.answer: Through their stories, art and dance
questions.explanation: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples have a deep connection with the land, expressed through their stories, art and dance.

questions.question: On what date did the First Fleet arrive in Australia?
questions.answer: 26 January 1788
questions.explanation: European settlement began when the First Fleet arrived from Great Britain on 26 January 1788 — the date now marked as Australia Day.

questions.question: How many convict ships made up the First Fleet?
questions.explanation: The First Fleet was 11 convict ships. Remember 11 ships in 1788.

questions.question: From which country did the First Fleet arrive?
questions.answer: Great Britain
questions.explanation: The First Fleet sailed from Great Britain. Early free settlers came from both Great Britain and Ireland.

questions.question: Who was the first Governor of the colony of New South Wales?
questions.answer: Captain Arthur Phillip
questions.explanation: Captain Arthur Phillip was the first Governor of the colony of New South Wales.

questions.question: Why did the British Government decide to transport convicts to New South Wales?
options: The convicts had volunteered to migrate
British jails could not hold the large number of people imprisoned
Australia had asked Britain for more workers
questions.answer: British jails could not hold the large number of people imprisoned
questions.explanation: British laws were harsh and the jails could not hold everyone imprisoned, so the government transported convicts to the new colony of New South Wales.

questions.question: Which was the first colony established by the British in Australia?
questions.answer: New South Wales
questions.explanation: New South Wales was the first colony the British established. More colonies followed in other parts of Australia.

questions.question: Where did most early free settlers come from?
questions.answer: Great Britain and Ireland
questions.explanation: Early free settlers came from Great Britain and Ireland, and that heritage shaped Australia's recent history, culture and politics.

questions.question: In which year did the gold rush begin in Australia?
questions.explanation: The gold rush began in 1851. Keep the four dates apart: 1788 settlement, 1851 gold, 1901 Federation, 1967 Referendum.

questions.question: Gold was first discovered in which two colonies?
questions.answer: New South Wales and Victoria
questions.explanation: Gold was discovered in the colonies of New South Wales and Victoria in 1851, drawing people from around the world.

questions.question: Which group were the first large group of migrants who did not come from Europe?
options: Vietnamese people arriving after World War II
Chinese people arriving during the gold rush
questions.answer: Chinese people arriving during the gold rush
questions.explanation: Chinese people arriving during the gold rush were the first large group of migrants who did not come from Europe.

questions.question: What happened to Australia's population in the 10 years after the gold rush began?
questions.answer: It more than doubled
questions.explanation: Australia's population more than doubled in the 10 years after gold was discovered.

questions.question: In what year did the separate colonies unite into a federation?
questions.explanation: In 1901 the separate colonies united into a federation. Federation is the union of colonies into one nation with the colonies keeping certain powers.

questions.question: What is the name of the federation of states formed in 1901?
options: The Colony of New South Wales
questions.answer: The Commonwealth of Australia
questions.explanation: The federation formed in 1901 is called the Commonwealth of Australia.

questions.question: Approximately what was Australia's population in 1901?
questions.answer: About four million
questions.explanation: Australia's population in 1901 was about four million — a figure that did not include Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples.

questions.question: What happened as a result of the 1967 Referendum?
options: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples were included in official estimates of the Australian population
Women were given the right to vote
questions.answer: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples were included in official estimates of the Australian population
questions.explanation: It was only after the 1967 Referendum that Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples were included in official estimates of the Australian population.

questions.question: A large wave of non-British migration came to Australia after which event?
questions.answer: World War II
questions.explanation: A wave of non-British migration followed World War II, when millions of Europeans had to leave their homelands.

questions.question: Which of the following was NOT established under the Australian Constitution in 1901?
questions.answer: The Australian Electoral Commission
questions.explanation: The Constitution established the national parliament, government and the High Court in 1901. The Australian Electoral Commission is a later Commonwealth agency, not a creation of the Constitution.

questions.question: What is Australia's national language?
questions.answer: English
questions.explanation: English is Australia's national language and part of the national identity, though other languages are also valued.

questions.question: Roughly how many distinct Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander languages are valued in Australia?
questions.answer: More than 100
questions.explanation: More than 100 distinct Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander languages are among the other languages Australia values.

questions.question: People from approximately how many countries have made Australia their home?
questions.answer: More than 200
questions.explanation: People from more than 200 countries have made Australia their home, making our society one of the most diverse in the world.

questions.question: Why should migrants learn and use English, according to the resource book?
options: Because it is required to enter Australia
To help them participate in Australian society
questions.answer: To help them participate in Australian society
questions.explanation: Migrants are encouraged to learn and use English because it helps them participate in Australian society and make the most of living and working here.

questions.question: How many states are there in Australia?
questions.answer: Six
questions.explanation: Australia has six states: New South Wales, Victoria, Queensland, Western Australia, South Australia and Tasmania.

questions.question: How many mainland territories does Australia have?
questions.answer: Two
questions.explanation: There are two mainland territories: the Australian Capital Territory and the Northern Territory.

questions.question: What is Australia's capital city?
questions.answer: Canberra
questions.explanation: Canberra is Australia's capital city, and each state and mainland territory has its own capital as well.

questions.question: What is the capital city of New South Wales?
questions.answer: Sydney
questions.explanation: Sydney is the capital of New South Wales and the nation's largest city.

questions.question: What is the capital city of Victoria?
questions.answer: Melbourne
questions.explanation: Melbourne is the capital of Victoria.

questions.question: What is the capital city of Queensland?
questions.answer: Brisbane
questions.explanation: Brisbane is the capital of Queensland.

questions.question: What is the capital city of Western Australia?
questions.answer: Perth
questions.explanation: Perth is the capital of Western Australia.

questions.question: What is the capital city of South Australia?
questions.answer: Adelaide
questions.explanation: Adelaide is the capital of South Australia.

questions.question: What is the capital city of Tasmania?
questions.answer: Hobart
questions.explanation: Hobart is the capital of Tasmania.

questions.question: What is the capital city of the Northern Territory?
questions.answer: Darwin
questions.explanation: Darwin is the capital of the Northern Territory.

questions.question: What is the capital city of the Australian Capital Territory?
questions.answer: Canberra
questions.explanation: Canberra is the capital of the Australian Capital Territory and of the nation.

questions.question: Which is Australia's largest state?
questions.answer: Western Australia
questions.explanation: Western Australia is the largest state. Queensland is second largest; Tasmania is smallest.

questions.question: Which is Australia's second largest state?
questions.answer: Queensland
questions.explanation: Queensland is the second largest state, after Western Australia.

questions.question: Which is Australia's smallest state?
questions.answer: Tasmania
questions.explanation: Tasmania is the smallest state. Victoria is the smallest of the mainland states — a common trap.

questions.question: Which is the smallest of the mainland states?
questions.answer: Victoria
questions.explanation: Victoria is the smallest of the mainland states. Tasmania is smaller but is not on the mainland.

questions.question: Which is the nation's largest city?
questions.answer: Sydney
questions.explanation: Sydney, the capital of New South Wales, is the nation's largest city. Canberra is the capital but not the largest.

questions.question: The Sydney Harbour Bridge and the Opera House are icons of which state?
questions.answer: New South Wales
questions.explanation: The Sydney Harbour Bridge and the Opera House are national icons, both in New South Wales.

questions.question: The Melbourne Cricket Ground, the 12 Apostles and the Royal Exhibition Building are icons of which state?
questions.answer: Victoria
questions.explanation: Victoria's icons include the Melbourne Cricket Ground, the 12 Apostles and the Royal Exhibition Building.

questions.question: Along which state's eastern coast does the Great Barrier Reef run?
questions.answer: Queensland
questions.explanation: The world-famous Great Barrier Reef runs along Queensland's eastern coast.

questions.question: The Ningaloo Coast, Margaret River and the Kimberley region are icons of which state?
questions.answer: Western Australia
questions.explanation: Western Australia's icons include the Ningaloo Coast, Margaret River and the Kimberley region.

questions.question: The Barossa Valley and the Flinders Ranges are icons of which state?
questions.answer: South Australia
questions.explanation: South Australia's icons include the Barossa Valley and the Flinders Ranges. The state has a rugged coastline and famous wine regions.

questions.question: Cradle Mountain, Port Arthur and the Bay of Fires are icons of which state?
questions.answer: Tasmania
questions.explanation: Tasmanian icons include Cradle Mountain, Port Arthur and the Bay of Fires.

questions.question: Uluru, Kata Tjuta and Kings Canyon are icons of which territory?
questions.answer: The Northern Territory
questions.explanation: Uluru, Kata Tjuta and Kings Canyon are Northern Territory icons.

questions.question: What separates Tasmania from the mainland?
questions.answer: The Bass Strait
questions.explanation: Tasmania is separated from the mainland by the Bass Strait. The Torres Strait is at the opposite end of the country.

questions.question: Where is the Australian Capital Territory located?
options: In the centre of the continent
questions.answer: Between Sydney and Melbourne
questions.explanation: The Australian Capital Territory sits between Sydney and Melbourne and holds the nation's capital, Canberra.

questions.question: Which national institutions are located in Canberra?
options: Parliament House and the High Court of Australia
The Australian Federal Police headquarters only
questions.answer: Parliament House and the High Court of Australia
questions.explanation: Parliament House and the High Court of Australia are among the national institutions located in Canberra.

questions.question: Who performs a Welcome to Country?
options: An Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander custodian of the local region
questions.answer: An Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander custodian of the local region
questions.explanation: A Welcome to Country is performed by an Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander custodian of the local region. Anyone can give an Acknowledgement of Country, but only a custodian can give a Welcome.

questions.question: Why was a Welcome to Country traditionally performed?
options: To ensure visitors had a safe and protected journey during their time on that land
To collect a fee from visitors
questions.answer: To ensure visitors had a safe and protected journey during their time on that land
questions.explanation: A Welcome to Country was traditionally performed to ensure visitors had a safe and protected journey during their time on that land.

questions.question: Which of the following is a form a Welcome to Country can take?
options: Songs, dances, smoking ceremonies or speeches
questions.answer: Songs, dances, smoking ceremonies or speeches
questions.explanation: A Welcome to Country can take many forms, including songs, dances, smoking ceremonies or speeches in traditional language or English.

questions.question: When does a Welcome to Country usually take place?
options: At the end of an event
It is usually the first item of proceedings to open an event
questions.answer: It is usually the first item of proceedings to open an event
questions.explanation: A Welcome to Country is usually the first item of proceedings, opening an event.

questions.question: Who can deliver an Acknowledgement of Country?
options: Only an Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander Elder
questions.answer: Anyone
questions.explanation: Anyone can deliver an Acknowledgement of Country — at meetings it is usually the Chair or Master of Ceremonies. Only a custodian performs a Welcome to Country.

questions.question: What is the purpose of an Acknowledgement of Country?
options: To recognise the gathering is on Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander land and pay respect to Traditional Custodians
questions.answer: To recognise the gathering is on Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander land and pay respect to Traditional Custodians
questions.explanation: An Acknowledgement of Country recognises that the gathering is on Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander land and pays respect to Traditional Custodians, particularly Elders past and present.

questions.question: On what date is Australia Day celebrated each year?
questions.answer: 26 January
questions.explanation: Australia Day is 26 January, the anniversary of the First Fleet's arrival in 1788.

questions.question: What does Australia Day mark the anniversary of?
options: The arrival of the First Fleet from Great Britain in 1788
questions.answer: The arrival of the First Fleet from Great Britain in 1788
questions.explanation: Australia Day marks the arrival of the First Fleet from Great Britain in 1788.

questions.question: Where is Australia Day a public holiday?
options: In every state and territory in Australia
Only in the Australian Capital Territory
questions.answer: In every state and territory in Australia
questions.explanation: Australia Day is a public holiday in every state and territory, and is the biggest annual public holiday in Australia.

questions.question: What does the Prime Minister announce in Canberra during Australia Day celebrations?
options: The Australian of the Year Awards
questions.answer: The Australian of the Year Awards
questions.explanation: The Prime Minister announces the Australian of the Year Awards in Canberra during Australia Day celebrations.

questions.question: On what date is Anzac Day commemorated each year?
questions.answer: 25 April
questions.explanation: Anzac Day is 25 April each year.

questions.question: What is Anzac Day named after?
options: The Australian and New Zealand Army Corps
The Australian National Zone and Coast
questions.answer: The Australian and New Zealand Army Corps
questions.explanation: Anzac is named after the Australian and New Zealand Army Corps.

questions.question: Where did the Anzacs land on 25 April 1915?
questions.answer: Gallipoli, in Türkiye
questions.explanation: The Anzacs landed at Gallipoli in Türkiye on 25 April 1915. Gallipoli is in Türkiye, not Greece.

questions.question: During which war did the Anzacs land at Gallipoli?
questions.answer: World War I
questions.explanation: The Gallipoli landing took place during World War I, on 25 April 1915.

questions.question: What do Australians remember on Anzac Day?
options: The arrival of the First Fleet
The sacrifice of all Australians who served and died in wars, conflicts and peacekeeping operations
questions.answer: The sacrifice of all Australians who served and died in wars, conflicts and peacekeeping operations
questions.explanation: Anzac Day remembers the sacrifice of all Australians who served and died in wars, conflicts and peacekeeping operations.

questions.question: What are the colours of the Australian National Flag?
questions.answer: Blue, white and red
questions.explanation: The Australian National Flag is blue, white and red. Green and gold are the national colours, not the flag's.

questions.question: What does the Union Jack in the top left corner of the Australian National Flag represent?
options: Our history of British settlement and the laws and institutions we inherited
questions.answer: Our history of British settlement and the laws and institutions we inherited
questions.explanation: The Union Jack represents our history of British settlement and the laws and institutions inherited as a result.

questions.question: How many points does the Commonwealth Star on the Australian National Flag have?
questions.answer: Seven
questions.explanation: The Commonwealth Star has seven points.

questions.question: What do the points of the Commonwealth Star represent?
options: One point for each of the six states and one point for the territories
questions.answer: One point for each of the six states and one point for the territories
questions.explanation: Six of the Commonwealth Star's points represent the six states, and the seventh represents the territories.

questions.question: What is the Southern Cross on the Australian National Flag?
options: A symbol of the six states
A group of stars that can be seen in the southern sky
questions.answer: A group of stars that can be seen in the southern sky
questions.explanation: The Southern Cross is a group of stars that can be seen in the southern sky.

questions.question: What are the colours of the Australian Aboriginal Flag?
questions.answer: Black, red and yellow
questions.explanation: The Australian Aboriginal Flag is black, red and yellow.

questions.question: What does the top half (black) of the Australian Aboriginal Flag represent?
questions.answer: The Aboriginal peoples of Australia
questions.explanation: The top half of the Aboriginal Flag is black and represents the Aboriginal peoples of Australia.

questions.question: What does the bottom half (red) of the Australian Aboriginal Flag represent?
options: The earth, which has ceremonial significance
questions.answer: The earth, which has ceremonial significance
questions.explanation: The bottom half is red and represents the earth, which has ceremonial significance.

questions.question: What does the yellow circle on the Australian Aboriginal Flag represent?
questions.answer: The sun
questions.explanation: The yellow circle on the Aboriginal Flag represents the sun.

questions.question: What are the colours of the Torres Strait Islander Flag?
questions.answer: Green, blue, black and white
questions.explanation: The Torres Strait Islander Flag is green, blue, black and white.

questions.question: What do the green stripes on the Torres Strait Islander Flag represent?
questions.answer: The land
questions.explanation: The green stripes represent the land; the blue panel represents the sea.

questions.question: What does the blue panel in the centre of the Torres Strait Islander Flag represent?
questions.answer: The sea
questions.explanation: The blue panel in the centre of the Torres Strait Islander Flag represents the sea.

questions.question: What do the black lines on the Torres Strait Islander Flag represent?
questions.answer: The Torres Strait Islander people
questions.explanation: The black lines represent the Torres Strait Islander people.

questions.question: What is the white shape in the centre of the Torres Strait Islander Flag?
options: A dancer's headdress, a symbol for all Torres Strait Islanders
questions.answer: A dancer's headdress, a symbol for all Torres Strait Islanders
questions.explanation: The white shape in the centre is a dancer's headdress, a symbol for all Torres Strait Islanders.

questions.question: What do the points of the white star on the Torres Strait Islander Flag represent?
options: The island groups in the Torres Strait
questions.answer: The island groups in the Torres Strait
questions.explanation: The points of the white star represent the island groups in the Torres Strait.

questions.question: What does the colour white symbolise on the Torres Strait Islander Flag?
questions.answer: Peace
questions.explanation: The colour white on the Torres Strait Islander Flag symbolises peace.

questions.question: What is the Commonwealth Coat of Arms?
options: The emblem of the state of New South Wales
The flag of the Australian Defence Force
The official symbol of the Commonwealth of Australia
questions.answer: The official symbol of the Commonwealth of Australia
questions.explanation: The Commonwealth Coat of Arms is the official symbol of the Commonwealth of Australia and identifies its authority and property.

questions.question: What does the shield in the centre of the Commonwealth Coat of Arms represent?
questions.answer: The six states and federation
questions.explanation: The shield in the centre of the Coat of Arms represents the six states and federation.

questions.question: Which two native animals support the shield on the Commonwealth Coat of Arms?
questions.answer: A kangaroo and an emu
questions.explanation: A kangaroo and an emu, both native Australian animals, support the shield on each side.

questions.question: What forms the background of the Commonwealth Coat of Arms?
questions.answer: The golden wattle
questions.explanation: The background of the Coat of Arms is the golden wattle, Australia's national flower.

questions.question: What is Australia's national flower?
questions.answer: The golden wattle
questions.explanation: The golden wattle is Australia's national flower, and each state and territory also has its own floral emblem.

questions.question: Where does the golden wattle grow mainly?
questions.answer: In south-eastern Australia
questions.explanation: The golden wattle is a small tree that grows mainly in south-eastern Australia, flowering golden yellow in spring.

questions.question: What are Australia's national colours?
questions.answer: Green and gold
questions.explanation: Australia's national colours are green and gold, and national sports teams usually wear them.

questions.question: Australia's national colours are the colours of which plant?
questions.answer: The golden wattle
questions.explanation: Green and gold are the colours of the golden wattle, Australia's national flower.

questions.question: What is Australia's national gemstone?
questions.answer: The opal
questions.explanation: The opal is Australia's national gemstone.

questions.question: According to Aboriginal legend, how were the colours of the opal created?
options: A star fell to the ground
The sun set over the desert
questions.answer: A rainbow touched the earth
questions.explanation: According to Aboriginal legend, a rainbow touched the earth and created the colours of the opal.

questions.question: What is Australia's national anthem?
questions.answer: 'Advance Australia Fair'
questions.explanation: 'Advance Australia Fair' is Australia's national anthem.

questions.question: When is Australia's national anthem sung?
options: On occasions of national importance, including citizenship ceremonies and major sporting events
questions.answer: On occasions of national importance, including citizenship ceremonies and major sporting events
questions.explanation: The anthem is sung on occasions of national importance, including citizenship ceremonies and major sporting events.

questions.question: What is the first line of 'Advance Australia Fair'?
options: Our home is girt by sea
questions.answer: Australians all let us rejoice
questions.explanation: The anthem opens with 'Australians all let us rejoice'.

questions.question: Which line follows 'Australians all let us rejoice' in the national anthem?
options: For we are one and free
Our home is girt by sea
We've golden soil and wealth for toil
questions.answer: For we are one and free
questions.explanation: The second line is 'For we are one and free'.

questions.question: Does each state and territory have its own flag?
options: No, only the Australian National Flag exists
Yes, each state and territory has its own flag
No, only the states have flags
questions.answer: Yes, each state and territory has its own flag
questions.explanation: Each state and territory has its own flag in addition to the Australian National Flag.

questions.question: Besides the Australian National Flag, which flags are officially recognised and may be flown in the community?
options: The Australian Aboriginal Flag and the Torres Strait Islander Flag
The Union Jack and the New Zealand flag
questions.answer: The Australian Aboriginal Flag and the Torres Strait Islander Flag
questions.explanation: The Australian Aboriginal Flag and the Torres Strait Islander Flag are also officially recognised and may be flown in the community.

questions.question: Does each state and territory have its own floral emblem?
options: Yes, each state and territory has its own floral emblem
No, only the golden wattle is used
questions.answer: Yes, each state and territory has its own floral emblem
questions.explanation: Each state and territory has its own floral emblem, alongside the national one, the golden wattle.

questions.question: What system of government does Australia have?
questions.answer: A parliamentary democracy
questions.explanation: Australia's system of government is a parliamentary democracy.

questions.question: In Australia's parliamentary democracy, where does the power of the government come from?
questions.answer: The Australian people
questions.explanation: The power of government comes from the Australian people, because citizens vote for people to represent them in parliament.

questions.question: To whom must representatives in parliament answer for the decisions they make?
questions.answer: The people, through elections
questions.explanation: Representatives must answer to the people, through elections, for the decisions they make.

questions.question: What does the Rule of Law mean?
options: Religious leaders are exempt from the law
No person, group or religious rule is above the law
The government can change laws without parliament
questions.answer: No person, group or religious rule is above the law
questions.explanation: The Rule of Law means no person, group or religious rule is above the law.

questions.question: Who must obey Australia's laws?
options: Everyone, including government, community and religious leaders, business people and the police
questions.answer: Everyone, including government, community and religious leaders, business people and the police
questions.explanation: Everyone must obey Australia's laws, including government, community and religious leaders, business people and the police.

questions.question: How do Australians believe change should occur?
options: Through discussion, peaceful persuasion and the democratic process
Only by decision of the King
questions.answer: Through discussion, peaceful persuasion and the democratic process
questions.explanation: Australians believe change should occur through discussion, peaceful persuasion and the democratic process.

questions.question: What is Australia's view on using violence to change a person's mind or the law?
options: Violence is acceptable in political protest
Violence is permitted if the cause is just
Australians reject violence as a way to change a person's mind or the law
questions.answer: Australians reject violence as a way to change a person's mind or the law
questions.explanation: Australians reject violence as a way to change a person's mind or the law.

questions.question: Australia's democratic system is based on which principle?
options: Every individual, regardless of background, has rights and equality under Australian law
Rights depend on a person's wealth
Only long-term residents have full rights
questions.answer: Every individual, regardless of background, has rights and equality under Australian law
questions.explanation: Australia's democratic system rests on the principle that every individual, regardless of background, has rights and equality under Australian law.

questions.question: Australians are expected to treat each other with dignity and respect regardless of which of the following?
options: Race, country of origin, gender, sexual orientation, marital status, age, disability, heritage, culture, politics, wealth or religion
questions.answer: Race, country of origin, gender, sexual orientation, marital status, age, disability, heritage, culture, politics, wealth or religion
questions.explanation: Australians are expected to treat each other with dignity and respect regardless of race, country of origin, gender, sexual orientation, marital status, age, disability, heritage, culture, politics, wealth or religion.

questions.question: What does freedom of speech mean in Australia?
options: People can say and write what they think and discuss their ideas with others, while obeying Australian laws
People can say anything, even if it breaks the law
questions.answer: People can say and write what they think and discuss their ideas with others, while obeying Australian laws
questions.explanation: Freedom of speech means people can say and write what they think and discuss ideas with others — while still obeying Australian laws.

questions.question: Are people in Australia allowed to criticise the government?
options: Yes, so long as they are still obeying Australian laws
No, criticising the government is illegal
Only members of parliament may do so
questions.answer: Yes, so long as they are still obeying Australian laws
questions.explanation: People can criticise the government, protest peacefully and campaign to change laws, provided they obey Australian laws.

questions.question: What does freedom of expression include?
options: Expressing views through art, film, music and literature
questions.answer: Expressing views through art, film, music and literature
questions.explanation: Freedom of expression covers expressing views through art, film, music and literature.

questions.question: What is freedom of association?
options: The right to travel anywhere in Australia
The right to a fair trial
The right to form and join associations to pursue common goals
questions.answer: The right to form and join associations to pursue common goals
questions.explanation: Freedom of association is the right to form and join associations to pursue common goals.

questions.question: Can a person in Australia be forced to join an organisation?
options: Yes, if the organisation is a trade union
Yes, if a court orders it
No, people can decide not to join and cannot be forced into doing so
questions.answer: No, people can decide not to join and cannot be forced into doing so
questions.explanation: People can decide not to join an organisation and cannot be forced into doing so.

questions.question: What must be true of a protest or public gathering in Australia?
options: It must be peaceful and must not injure any person or damage property
It must be approved by the King
It must be held only on weekends
questions.answer: It must be peaceful and must not injure any person or damage property
questions.explanation: Gatherings and protests must be peaceful and must not injure any person or damage property.

questions.question: What religious heritage does the resource book say Australia has?
questions.answer: A Judaeo-Christian heritage
questions.explanation: Australia has a Judaeo-Christian heritage, though people from all the large religions live here.

questions.question: Which of these are Christian days on which Australia has public holidays?
options: Good Friday, Easter Sunday and Christmas Day
questions.answer: Good Friday, Easter Sunday and Christmas Day
questions.explanation: Australia has public holidays on Christian days such as Good Friday, Easter Sunday and Christmas Day.

questions.question: What does it mean that the government in Australia is secular?
options: It operates separately from churches or other religious entities
questions.answer: It operates separately from churches or other religious entities
